summary: CAGED pentatonic colours notes with a box that is not on the neck
detail: The penta branch uses the unfiltered placements for owners (line ~682) and for cagedShapesShown (~665), while the box stepper gets placements.filter(onNeck) (~701). The scale branch filters in all three places and carries the comment explaining why. Verified A/B, chord C in C major: penta legend reads "D shape 0-1 . 9-13", scale reads "D shape 9-13" - the 0-1 run comes from a D@-2 box you cannot step to.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. Pentatonic filters the box list once, at the source, and uses that one list for the owners, for cagedShapesShown and for the stepper - the asymmetry was the bug: the arrows were already filtered, so the legend advertised a run nothing could reach. Scales had the same fault in the one place it did not filter, the nearest-box fallback that colours a note no box owns, and is now filtered once at the source too. Verified A/B on C in C major: penta read "D shape 0-1 . 9-13" and now reads "D shape 9-13", matching scales exactly. Covered by a test comparing the runs the legend names against the windows the arrows actually reach, in both views.

summary: A power-voiced rhythm has no dominant-7th grip and silently plays a full barre
detail: STYLE_TABLE.power has no '7' key, so voiceChord falls through to barre['7']. Swept all genre progressions x rhythms; one live case: Blues -> "Quick change in G" under "Shuffle riff (5-6)", where G7/C7/D7 are voiced and tabbed as six-string E/A-shape dominant barres at frets 3, 8 and 10 in a drive-toned riff meant to be power chords.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. Power and octave styles no longer fall back to the barre table for a quality they do not list: their grips hold root, 5th and octave and have no 3rd or 7th to alter, so every quality plays the same shape. Wider than logged - m7 and maj7 were affected too, and the octave style had the identical fault. Verified on the reported case, Chicago blues / Quick change in G / Shuffle riff (5-6): G7, C7 and D7 were six-string dominant barres at frets 3, 8 and 10 and are now three-string power chords at 3/5/5, 8/10/10 and 5/7/7. Sweeping every genre progression against every power or octave rhythm, chords voicing a 3rd or 7th went from 76 to 0, which is now a test.

summary: The 'm/maj7' chord alias is unreachable
detail: parseChordName's regex treats / as the slash-chord separator and the bass group only accepts [A-Ga-g], so "Cm/maj7" never parses. The mmaj7, minmaj7 and m(maj7) aliases still work, so no chord is actually unnameable.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. parseChordName gives the whole tail after the root its chance to name a chord before reading a trailing "/G" as a bass note, so a slash inside a suffix no longer splits the name. Wider than logged: 6/9 was unreachable the same way, since "/9" is not a bass note either. Verified Cm/maj7 and C6/9 now parse, that every slash chord still parses as one (C/G, Am/C, F#m/A, Cmaj7/E, Bb/D, Cm/G, C7/E), and that bad input is still refused (H, C/H, Cxyz, C/, C/Gm, empty). Five assertions added to the theory suite.

summary: No BPM preset chip is highlighted at page load
detail: The tempo starts at 60 and a 60 chip exists, but the highlight is only applied in the tempo input's 'input' handler, which does not fire at load. A shared link does set it, because applyShareState dispatches the event.
resolution: Fixed and verified closed 2026-09-07. The 60 chips carry class="active" in the markup and the tempo input's own default is 60, so the two agree at load; a shared link carrying a different tempo re-syncs them because applyShareState dispatches the input event. Verified at load (both 60 chips lit, tempo 60), on a t=90 link (both 90 chips lit, 60 cleared) and on a t=138 link (no chip lit, which is correct - 138 is not a preset).

summary: Measure readout flashes "1" for about 50 ms when count-in is off
detail: With the count-in off, playbackStartTime is still currentTime + 0.05, so syncHighlight's count-in branch is true for the first few frames and prints a clamped beat number.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. countInFrom is null when there is no count-in, and syncHighlight's count-in branch checks it, so the 50ms gap before the first chord is no longer read as a count-in to display. Verified by reading rather than by observation: the readout is driven by requestAnimationFrame, which the browser freezes while the pane is hidden, so the transition cannot be watched from here.

summary: boxIndex and heldWindow persist across mode changes and re-rolls
detail: Neither is reset when the key changes or a new progression is rolled, so a held window from an old key can carry into an unrelated one. boxIndex is also shared between the arp, penta and scale views, which have different box counts. Arguably intended for Hold position; worth a decision either way.
resolution: Closed 2026-09-07, no longer applicable. heldWindow went with "Hold position" in B26. What remains is positionAnchor, and holding the position across a key change, a re-roll or a change of view is now the designed behaviour B22 asked for, not a leak: measured on C major stepped to frets 6-10, the position stays 6-10 through a key change to F# major and lands within 6-10 to 8-10 in all five views. The stale-index worry is gone too - applyBoxWindow re-picks the box nearest the anchor and wraps the index into range, so an index from a view with more boxes cannot point off the end of one with fewer.

summary: Preset variant highlight desyncs when the key leaves the variant's mode
detail: Choose Blues -> "Minor blues" (mode: minor), then switch to a major key: the progression stays but variantIdx still points at a minor-only variant, so no variant button is marked active.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. renderPresetVariants now drops a selection whose variant the current mode has no room for, the same rule buildPresetSelect already applies one level up to a preset. The progression is untouched - its degrees transpose as before - so the chart keeps playing and the picker simply stops claiming a preset it no longer matches. Clearing rather than re-pointing is the honest answer: Minor blues is 0x4 3x2 0x2 5x1 4x1 0x1 4x1 and 12-bar is 0x4 3x2 0x2 4x1 3x1 0x1 4x1, so naming the nearest surviving variant would misdescribe what is on the chart. Verified on the reported case - Blues/Minor blues in A minor, switched to C major - the picker reads None and the chords stay as transposed, VI included. A variant that fits both modes, 12-bar, survives the same trip still selected and still marked. Swept 36 preset selections and 22 variant clicks across four keys with no selection clearing itself and exactly one variant marked throughout.

summary: shownVoicings is assigned before its let declaration
detail: runChordFinder assigns shownVoicings at ~line 496; the let is at ~line 506. It works because the assignment only ever runs from an event handler after module load, but it is a TDZ trap for anyone who calls runChordFinder at load time.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. The let moved above runChordFinder, next to a note saying what the list is for. It never bit, because the only assignment runs from an event handler long after load, but the declaration sat ten lines below its own assignment. Verified the finder still draws (22 shapes for Am7) and cards still strum.

summary: A chord previewed behind the others appeared somewhere else once selected
detail: Reported by Jeff with two screenshots: with D in front, E was previewed at frets 7-9 in root position; selecting E gave 4-5, 2nd inversion. Two causes. The preview aimed at the middle of the drawn window while a chord change aimed at the position anchor, and those differ once the window has been padded to a hand span and stretched to cover the other chords. And a render that picked its box by index - changing string set, for one - left the anchor stale, so the next chord change jumped to wherever the anchor still pointed.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. The preview aims at the anchor, the same fret a chord change aims at, so the two choose from the same list against the same target. And the anchor now follows the box on any render that picked it by index, staying put only when a chord change chose it - which is the case the walk fix needed. Covered by a test comparing, for every chord in every position, the notes it is drawn with behind the others against the notes it is drawn with in front: 463 comparisons.

summary: Chords in one position dropped a chord whose grip reached past the box
detail: Reported by Jeff: Am-Dm-E at the nut, position frets 0-2, drew Am and E but no Dm. A CAGED grip is four frets wide and a box down at the nut can be three, so the strict "only a shape lying wholly inside the window" rule silently drops a chord - the open Dm is 0-3 against a window of 0-2. B20 fixed exactly this for Triads and I left Chords on the strict rule, reasoning that CAGED grips are dense enough; they are not, at the nut.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. Chords uses the same nearest-shape rule Triads does, and the readout widens to cover what is drawn. Then, per Jeff, the selection was restructured so the preview and the real thing cannot disagree: one nearestShape() picks for every view, and each view builds its shape list once - chordShapes() for Chords, triadShapes() for Triads - used both for the box the position lands on and for the chords drawn behind. That fixed a second mismatch the tests caught, where the two lists were sorted differently and equidistant shapes broke ties opposite ways. The "whole progression is on the neck" test now covers both views and walks up from the nut.

summary: "Hold position" silently removed notes, and in Triads removed the chord
detail: Jeff asked when it had an effect. Measured on Am-Dm-E across all four views: Chords clipped Dm from 4 notes to 3, Pentatonic and Scales lost notes on chords that were fine a moment before, and Triads drew the chord in front with zero notes, dropping the progression to two chords. It pinned the literal fret window rather than the position, so a shape needing a fret just outside got clipped - the same class of fault as B17/B19/B25, surviving in the one place still doing it.
resolution: Removed 2026-09-07 on Jeff's call. Keeping the position across a chord change is what the anchor does now, in every view, without being asked - so the control had no purpose left beyond the clipping. The heldWindow plumbing goes with it.

summary: The position arrows were disabled in voice leading
detail: Reported by Jeff. Voice leading chained from the first chord's lowest shape with no way to move it, so the arrows were greyed out - but there is an obvious thing for them to do.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. The first chord now takes whichever box the arrows are on and the rest follow it, so stepping moves the whole walk up or down the neck. Verified in all three methods: the drawn span moves as you step.

summary: Cluster and Voice leading drew the same shapes as One box but rendered them differently
detail: Reported by Jeff with two screenshots of Am-Dm-E in Chords / in one position: the legend named identical shapes (Am i [E] 5-7, Dm iv [A] 5-7, E V [C] 4-7) but the neck looked different depending on which position method was lit. His diagnosis was right - Cluster and Voice leading were still running the old Progression renderer, inherited when the modes were merged and never updated. Measured side by side: One box drew the chord in front lit with the rest as ghosts at 1/0.4/0.07 and a "position: frets X-Y" readout; Cluster and Voice leading drew the positions-mode tiers (0.22 at rest, with only each chord's lowest root at full strength), split shared dots in two, and had no fret readout at all. Voice leading had two implementations - the reachable one in the old branch and voiceLedBoxIndex(), which the branch above it meant nothing ever called.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. The tier, label and shared-cell logic came out into one placeShape(), which ghostMarkers() and the cluster branch both draw through, so all three methods produce the same picture and differ only in where each chord's shape lands - which they still do, in 79 of 90 progression/position/arpeggio combinations measured. The old renderer went with it: posLegendData, the positions-mode and pos-follow CSS, pos-root, ringed, split dots, data-rootfor and paintPositionsFollow(), plus the unreachable voiceLedBoxIndex()/cagedBoxesFor() pair. Following playback now needs no repaint - the tiers are in the markers. Covered by a test asserting the shared contract over 54 readings, checked red/green by reinstating the positions-mode class.

summary: A shared link pasted into an already-open tab restores nothing
detail: applyShareState runs once, from the practice tab's init. tabs.js listens for hashchange and popstate, but its handler only calls goTo(), which returns early when the target tab is already active - and it never re-reads the state half of the fragment. So opening a shared link in a new tab works, and pasting one into the address bar of a tab already sitting on #caged-practice silently does nothing: key, chords and tempo all stay as they were. Verified by writing a share hash with the Share button, disturbing the key and tempo, then restoring the hash and firing hashchange: all three fields kept the disturbed values. Back/forward across two shared progressions has the same fault.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. The practice tab now listens for hashchange and popstate and re-reads the state half of the fragment, stopping playback first so the old progression does not carry on underneath. Its own writes go through history.replaceState, which fires neither event, so there is no loop. Verified by taking two real share links, navigating to a bare #caged-practice and then pasting each link back into the same tab: key, tempo and chords all came back. Note the first attempt at this check proved nothing - it set location.hash to the value it already held, which fires no event at all.

summary: The Chords section had a sentence cut off mid-clause and a duplicated description
detail: Three defects found while re-reading the docs against the code. The sentence "the toggle changes how much you see rather than what you're looking at, and the" ended there and ran straight into the next paragraph - ff5f210 had continued it with a clause about the Box row that a later edit truncated. The "in one position" description then said the same thing twice, once as "the chord that's sounding lit, and the rest of the changes drawn in behind it" and again as "the whole progression gathered into one place, drawn the way it plays", reading as a merge artefact. And the reading toggle was named as **Show**; the control has been called **View** since T20.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. The clause is restored in current terminology (the Position row works in both readings; with the grips alone each grip is its own box), the duplicated half is dropped, and the toggle is named **View**.

summary: The variant row kept the previous preset's buttons after it hid
detail: Found while sweeping the B11 fix. renderPresetVariants sets presetVariantRow.hidden and returns before emptying presetVariantGroup, so a preset with fewer than two variants for the current mode leaves the last preset's buttons in the DOM with their click handlers attached. Not reachable by pointer, since the row is hidden - but a stale Minor blues button survived into a major key this way and my own sweep clicked it, flipping the key to minor mid-test and making the fix look as though it were clearing presets it should have kept.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-07. The group is emptied before the early return, so a hidden row holds nothing. Verified across four keys and every preset: no hidden row holds a button.

summary: The position jumped between chords in Chords, one position, with Whole arpeggio on
detail: Reported 2026-09-08 with screenshots: C major, Three-chord I-IV-V, All chords in one position, One box, Whole arpeggio. Switching which chord was in front moved the box - C at 10-13, F at 12-15, G at 10-12 at the same step - while the same progression with the arpeggio off held one window for every chord. The grips reading is steady because it draws each other chord's nearest grip as a ghost and then covers what it drew, so the window is a union that comes out the same whichever chord is lit; the arpeggio reading drew its ghosts as chord tones clipped to the window, which can never push it outward, so the window stayed whatever the lit chord's own arpeggio box happened to be. Those boxes are wider and there are fewer of them (three, with the default A/E/D), so each chord's nearest to the same anchor could be a couple of frets from the last.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-08. The arpeggio reading in one position now takes its window from the grips - the same boxes the arpeggio-off reading steps through - and then widens it to take in the nearest grip of every chord in the progression, which is the union the grips reading arrives at by drawing. Extracted as coverProgressionGrips() so the two readings share the idea of where the hand is rather than each inventing one. The arpeggio then fills that window. Verified: the window is now identical for every chord at every position, and identical to the arpeggio-off window at the same step, across C major, A minor and Eb minor and all three position methods. A sweep of 40 configuration groups (2 keys x 5 views x neck/position x arpeggio on/off, stepping 3 positions and cycling every chord, hashing the drawn SVG and the legend) changed exactly the 2 groups it should - caged/position/arpeggio-on for each key - and left the other 38 byte-identical. Tests 246/246.

summary: x-x-4-4-5-5 (A E B F#) was named B7sus4, never A6/9
detail: Reported 2026-09-10 with a screenshot of the reverse finder: D4 G4 B5 e5 - A, E, B, F# - listed B7sus4, B11 and F#m11, when any chord chart calls that shape A6/9 (fachords, jamplay). The 6/9 formula had the 3rd in its essential tones, so a shape without the C# could never be a 6/9, and the chord finder could not offer the shape for A6/9 either. Guitarists name the 6/9 without its 3rd as a matter of course - x-x-2-2-3-3 is G6/9 in every method book.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. The 6/9's essential tones are now root, 6th and 9th, with a new anyOf rule asking for at least one of the 3rd and the 5th on top - a bare A, F#, B is still not a 6/9. identifyChords and the voicing search both honour anyOf. A E B F# now reads A6/9 first with B7sus4 still listed after it; C E A D (the jazz form without the 5th) is still C6/9; A F# B alone is nothing. The chord finder offers x-x-4-4-5-5 for A6/9, x-x-2-2-3-3 for G6/9 and x-3-2-2-3-3 for C6/9, all pinned in CANON_PRESENT. While checking other chords a chart names loosely: 9sus4 is now a chord type (a 7sus4 with the 9th, what an 11 chord is nearly always played as), add2 reads as add9, 6add9 as 6/9, and brackets are ignored so C7(#9), Cm7(b5) and C(add9) parse. Tests 320/320.

summary: x-x-5-6-7-7 (G C# F# B) matched no chord at all - it is a rootless A13
detail: Reported 2026-09-10 with a screenshot: D5 G6 B7 e7 gave 'No standard chord name matches these notes yet.' The notes are the b7, 3, 13 and 9 of A - the rootless 13th every jazz and funk player uses, the bass having the root (fachords lists it under A13). identifyChords only ever tried the notes that were sounding as roots, so a chord whose root is absent could never be named, and the chord finder could never draw one.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. identifyChords now tries the twelve roots that are not sounding as well, for chords of five tones or more, requiring every essential tone but the root and the 9th (flat or sharp, but not a minor 3rd dressed as a #9) standing in for it; such matches are flagged rootless, named '(no root)' in the reverse finder, and listed after the readings that contain their root. B F# C# G reads 'A13 (no root)' and nothing else; C# E G B is C#m7b5 first and A9 (no root) after; E G B is only ever Em, and C E G D is Cadd9 rather than an Am11 with two notes gone. The chord finder generates the matching voicings - four different notes on the top four strings, within two frets, the guide tones and the 9th among them, no open strings - keeps them out of the position-by-position pass so they cannot displace the everyday shapes, and lets the best two in by rank, captioned 'no root' with a tooltip that says rootless. A13 shows x-x-5-6-7-7 and x-x-4-4-2-3. Tests 320/320.

summary: The Hendrix chord x-3-2-3-4-x was never offered; only x-3-2-3-4-0 was
detail: Found 2026-09-10 while splitting the finder into common and less common shapes. The 'thinner copy' rule treated a shape that is a picked shape minus some open strings as a variant not worth showing, so C7#9's x-3-2-3-4-x - the shape everyone plays - was hidden behind x-3-2-3-4-0, which has the open E thrown in because it happens to be in the chord. The same rule hid nothing else canonical, but the selection pass had the same blind spot for movable grips generally: 5-x-4-4-5-5 (root in the bass, one string skipped) and x-x-4-4-5-5 (no root in the bass) were both thrown out for A6/9.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10 as part of the common/less-common work. A shape left with no open strings is no longer a thinner copy of one that has them - it is movable where its parent works at one fret - and the second pass admits movable grips of a known kind (barre, root-6/root-5 grip, top-string voicing, shell, triad) whether or not the root is underneath or a string is skipped, a few of each kind, judged by what makes that kind good (a barre by fullness, a grip as a four-note thing, a top-string voicing without credit for a root in the bass). Two shapes that are one hand - same fingers on the shared strings, both movable or neither, both with a wide barre or neither - show as one, preferring the recognised grip and then the fuller one, except that a grip wants one string per note of the chord: 3-x-3-4-3-x is the G7 grip, 5-x-4-4-5-5 the A6/9 one. One BASELINE entry was changed by hand for that reason: Cm7's 8-6-8-8-8-6 became 8-x-8-8-8-6, the same hand with the 5th string muted rather than barred. Tests 320/320.

summary: A 13th chord's 2nd was labelled 2, not 9
detail: Found 2026-09-10 while building the ear trainer, which writes its answer buttons with the same degree names the diagrams use: Bb13 offered "C 2" alongside "G 13". degreeNameFor only promoted a 2 to a 9 when the chord's own name contained a 9, so a chord named 11 or 13 - both of which contain a 9 - read its 2nd as a 2. Same for the 11th of a 13 chord, though this app's 13 formula carries no 11 so that case never came up.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. An extension names the ones below it: a 2 reads as a 9 when the name holds 9, 11 or 13, and a 5 reads as an 11 when it holds 11 or 13. Checked against every formula that has digits in its name - 7b5, m7b5, 7sus4 and 9sus4 all still read their 4ths and 5ths plainly, since the test is for the extension number and not for any digit. A plain sus2 still reads 2. The ear trainer's test pins Bb13 having no bare 2 in it, and Csus2 having one.

summary: No answer matched in any of the three note drills
detail: Reported 2026-09-10: in the Chord drill the note sounded two octaves above the root, and pressing the root button said 'not that one'. The octave was a red herring - since the chord-quality drill landed that morning, no answer in any of the three note drills matched anything at all. Adding that drill made the answer buttons generic: each carries a data-key, and answer() compares it to asked.key. The quality drill set a key on what it asked; the note drills went on setting `asked` to the note object itself, which has a pitch class and no key, so every comparison was against undefined. The score kept counting the misses, which is what made it look like a scoring or an octave problem rather than a total one.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. The question is now taken from the same list the buttons are built from - choicesOf(subject) - rather than worked out separately, so there is no second place for the two to disagree about what an answer is called. The note drills keep the note beside the choice for the cells to sound. The lasting fix is the test, since nothing about either half was wrong in isolation: js/tests-ear.js builds the controls the tab binds to, the way tests-practice.js does, and works all four drills - eight questions each, every button pressed, exactly one accepted - plus the score counting questions rather than presses, and Back restoring a whole question. Reinstating the bug fails two of the three loudly. The runner also catches a throwing suite now and reports it as a failure: the first attempt at reinstating the bug threw instead, and took the whole page down with it, which said less than a red line would have.

summary: The Voice toggle did nothing in any style but Simple
detail: Reported 2026-09-10 while auditioning the new piano: "the piano/guitar voice toggle on the practice tab doesn't seem to do anything". It did work, but only under the Simple style. Simple has its own beat scheduler (scheduleSimpleBeat in practice.js), which passed chordVoice to playChord; every other style - Rock, Blues, Jazz, Pop, Funk - comps through playStyleVoice, which took the style's spelling of the chord (triad / dom7 / jazz shell) and never took the voice at all, so those styles always played piano whatever the toggle said. Introduced by T49, which added the toggle to the one path it was tested on. Nothing caught it because a chord in the wrong voice is still a chord: it sounds fine, it is just the wrong instrument.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. Every chord in the app now goes through one playVoicedNotes(freqs, time, duration, velocity, voice), so the voice can't reach one kind of chord and miss another: playChord and playChord7 are both thin wrappers over it, and each STYLE_VOICES entry carries the voice down. New test: every style in the library is asked to play a chord with the guitar voice and has to pass it to the thing that would strum it - sound isn't testable, but the choice arriving is, and playVoicedNotes records it before scheduling a note so the test needs no audio context. Sabotaged the jazz entry back to the broken form and watched it fail first.

summary: In the Simple style a chord rang over the next two, so the downbeat filled the bar
detail: Reported 2026-09-10: "the first piano hit of each bar fills the whole bar, it should stop when the next hit starts". scheduleSimpleBeat asked for a duration of interval * 2.3 - a hit rang 2.3 times the gap to the next one, so at quarter notes every chord sounded under the following two. It had been there a long time and was defensible while every voice was synthesized: that piano's two-stage decay had fallen away to almost nothing by the next beat, so the overlap read as ring rather than as blur. The recorded piano actually sustains, which turned the same rule into one chord smeared across the bar.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. A hit now lasts exactly until the next one is struck, through a named simpleHitSeconds() so the rule is stated once. The envelope already tapers over the last third of a note, so the fade lands as the next hit arrives instead of being chopped. Measured: the output now drops 33-66% into the beat before the next attack, where before it did not drop at all. New test walks six tempos by three note values and fails any hit that outlasts its gap; watched it fail against the old 2.3x.

summary: The piano kept sounding after pause
detail: Reported 2026-09-10: "the piano also sustains after I press pause, make it stop". cancelScheduled stopped notes that hadn't started and deliberately left sounding ones to ring out "the way they would have" - right when every voice was synthesized and gone in a moment, wrong for a recorded piano note that rings for seconds. Measured before the fix: a chord cancelled mid-ring was still at 88% of its level 40ms later and 45% a full second later.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. Every voice now hands startVoice the gain node that carries it - twelve call sites, every instrument and drum - and stopping ramps a sounding voice to silence over 60ms before stopping the node: long enough not to click, short enough to be the button you pressed. Measured after: the same chord falls to 13% within 40ms, and what continues is the reverb decaying like a room. cancelScheduled now reports how many notes it called off and how many it faded, which is what let the test drive both paths without anything having to listen; sabotaged the fade away and watched it fail.

summary: Bass lines sat too high, because every root was taken in the same octave
detail: Reported 2026-09-10: "in a lot of the styles, the bass hits high notes that a real bass player doesn't hit often". bassFreqAt was always called with octave 2, so how far the root sat from the bottom of the instrument depended entirely on the key - a C sat at MIDI 36 and a B at 47 - and anything built on top of the root climbed from there. A boogie figure that fits comfortably in C reached A3 in B. The jazz walking line made it worse by taking its third an octave up (offsets 15/16), which is not what a walking line does.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. A player takes the lowest root they have, so roots from E up take octave 1 and C, C#, D, D# take octave 2, which puts every root inside E1-D#2 whatever the key. The walking line's third is now in position (+3/+4) rather than an octave up. Measured across every style, variant, root and next-root: the bass now spans D#1-D#3 where it used to reach A3, and most styles sit in E1-D#2 - only the punk and disco octave figures go above D#2, which is where those lines belong. New test pins the register itself (23,328 notes) so a style added later can't quietly write a bass part up where a player wouldn't go; sabotaged the octave rule back to the old one and watched it fail.

summary: The bass warm did not cover the bottom of the register
detail: Noticed 2026-09-10 while checking a report of "I feel like I'm getting some synth bass". warmBass filtered samples with spec.hi >= 33, which happened to cover the old register exactly and covered nothing below it. With the roots moved down to E1 (B41) the lowest samples - pizz_g1, covering MIDI 28-31 - were outside the filter, so those notes would have played on the synthesized bass no matter how long you waited, and only in the keys that reach them.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. The warmed stretch is now a stated range, BASS_RANGE 26-52, used by both the warm and the test, and all three velocity bands are fetched rather than two - the whole thing is 23 files where the piano is 25, and the difference is not worth the hole it leaves. The test now checks not only that every bass note a style can play has a sample, but that the sample is one the warm actually loads; narrowed the filter back to 33 and watched it name pizz_g1_ma.wav. Also added a running tally of which voices actually played (GT.audio.voiceUse), because "am I hearing the samples?" should be a measurement: across Simple, Blues and Jazz it now reports every piano and bass note sampled and none synthesized.

summary: In Simple quarter notes the downbeat jarred against the other beats
detail: Reported 2026-09-10: "the difference between the first beat and the rest is really jarring - am I maybe getting synth piano on the first beat, or is it using different samples for the louder beat?". Not synth: the tally says every note was sampled. It was the second guess. The Simple style struck the downbeat at velocity 1 and everything else at 0.62, and the piano's velocity layers split at 0.63 - so beat one came off the hard-strike recordings (C3vH and friends) and beats two to four off the soft ones, measured 4.4 dB apart at the peak. The layers are two different strikes, not one strike at two volumes, so a bar alternated between two instruments as well as two volumes.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10 in two halves. The layers now cross-fade: velocities within 0.15 of the split play both recordings with equal-power gains, so the strike changes gradually instead of switching. sin/cos rather than the obvious sqrt pair - both hold the power constant, but sqrt has infinite slope at nought and so would have moved the lurch to the edge of the window rather than removing it, which the new test caught on the first run. And the accent itself is now 0.86 against 0.68, a named SIMPLE_ACCENT rather than two inline numbers: measured 2.5 dB where it was 4.9, with the downbeat on the hard layer and the other beats sharing most of it. Test pins the size of the accent, that both velocities land in the overlap, and that the mix is continuous and equal-power all the way across; sabotaged it back to a threshold and watched it name velocity 0.63.

summary: The jazz comp climbed into the top of the piano in sharp keys
detail: Reported 2026-09-10: "I'm getting some really high pitched piano notes in swing, can you make it stay closer to the centre of the piano". chord7Frequencies builds a voicing upward from its lowest note, starting at octave 4 for the rootless jazz shape, so where it finished depended entirely on the key: E4-C5 in C, G#4-E5 in E, and up to Ab5 in Ab. The dominant-7th voicing had the same problem an octave lower - C7 sat C3-A#3 while B7 sat B3-A4 - so the comp wandered by nearly an octave depending on which chord came up.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-10. Every 7th voicing is now settled by whole octaves until its centre sits within a half-octave of A3: the shape and the spacing are untouched, only the register moves, which is what a player does when a grip lands too high. Centre rather than ceiling on purpose - a ceiling alone leaves neighbouring keys an octave apart, since a voicing that just fits stays put while the one a semitone above it drops. Measured over all twelve roots and eight qualities: the jazz voicings now span B2-F4 where they used to reach G#5, and every voicing's centre lands between MIDI 51 and 63. Plain triads are untouched; they never left the middle. PIANO_RANGE narrowed to 45-72 to match, which is fewer samples to warm.

summary: The audio engine ran for ever after playback stopped, costing battery on a locked iPad
detail: Reported 2026-09-11: an iPad left with the page open was draining a lot of battery overnight. The wake lock was innocent - it is taken on play and released on stop - and both schedulers clear their timers, and both requestAnimationFrame loops return unless something is playing. The AudioContext was the problem: created on the first interaction and never suspended, so it went on rendering its graph at 375 blocks a second, through the limiter and the reverb convolver that are permanently wired up, for as long as the tab stayed open. Measured: after stopping playback the state was still "running" and the audio clock was still advancing three seconds later, with nothing audible. On iOS a live audio session also keeps the page resident, so the tab never settles.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11. The context is suspended when nothing has sounded for twenty seconds and resumed by the next note - the clock doesn't advance while suspended, so a note scheduled a moment ahead is still a moment ahead when it starts. A hidden page waits only six seconds, long enough for a ringing sample to finish, since nobody is listening to a tab they can't see; pagehide suspends at once, which is what iOS sends when the screen locks even where it skips visibilitychange. Measured after: idle for 20s suspends and the clock stops, a note wakes it and sounds, a hidden page suspends within 7s, and 28 seconds of continuous playback stayed running throughout with the clock advancing 4.0s per 4s and notes arriving at a steady 32 per 4s. The rule about when to sleep is a pure function with its own test, because the worst version of this bug is an engine that sleeps mid-progression. Revised the same day, after asking what the twenty seconds was actually buying: nothing, as it turned out, and the window was hiding a flaw. It was measured from when a note STARTED, so it had to be longer than the longest a note can ring - a whole-note chord at 40 BPM rings 6.06s - or the engine would freeze a note mid-decay and thaw it, still sounding, when it next woke. Six seconds for a hidden page was inside that by 0.06s. Now startVoice watches each voice's own stop() call, so the engine knows when the sound actually ends and the windows only have to cover what they are for: ten seconds visible (so it doesn't cycle between two clicks in the finder or two ear-training questions - waking measured at 1.5-5.6ms here, but an audio session transition is not free on a phone) and one second hidden. Measured: a six-second chord on a hidden page keeps the engine running for 7 seconds and suspends on the 8th, where the old rule would have cut it off at 6.

summary: The suggested part changed on every loop through the chords
detail: Reported 2026-09-11 on first use of T54: "the part is changing on every loop through the chords". Two causes, one on top of the other. The neck follows the playing chord, and in one position that re-picks the box on every change; the part was re-realised whenever the neck redrew with a different window, so each chord got the part realised into that chord's box - different notes every time round. And underneath that, an ordering bug: the signature that decides whether to rebuild was stored BEFORE the fills were rolled, so it described a part that no longer existed, and the very next redraw saw "different fills" and rebuilt once more - which is how the part was carried off into whatever window the neck had moved to by then, even with the window taken out of the signature.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11. The window is no longer part of what triggers a rebuild: the part is realised in the window it was set in and stays there; stepping the box yourself (the arrows, or the window on the neck, which forwards to them) is the one neck change that moves it, and that is wired to those controls rather than to the neck's redraw. The signature is taken after the fills are rolled, at the end of the rebuild. Test drives the neck to a different box the way the follow does and holds the part still, then steps the box and checks it moved; put the signature back before the roll and watched it fail. Found with a trace on the rebuild, not by reasoning: the signatures read identical from outside, because the reading was taken after the roll.

summary: The tab playhead never appeared, in the part tab or the genre examples
detail: Found 2026-09-11 while adding an indicator of the current position to the part's tab, which turned out to exist already and never show. Both tabs showed it with head.hidden = false. An SVG element has no `hidden` property - it is HTMLElement's, and SVGElement doesn't inherit it - so the assignment made an expando and left the attribute in place, and the [hidden]{display:none} rule kept the playhead invisible. The genre examples have had this since the tab was written.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11: removeAttribute / setAttribute in both places. Measured in a visible pane: the playhead appears when the progression starts, moves slot by slot, and is hidden again on stop.

summary: The suggested part was inaudible under the band
detail: Reported 2026-09-11 as two things: "New fills isn't doing anything" and "add an ability to have the tab part play audio". New fills was working - twelve presses gave six or seven distinct rolls, every one realised differently - but nobody could hear it: measured, the part at the guitar's own level added 0.5 dB to the mix. Fourteen notes played, none audible over piano, bass and kit.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11. The part sits on top of the band the way a lead does: a level of its own, measured at 2.4 dB added to the mix, the part alone about 85% of the band's level, peaks at 0.86 under the limiter. And a Sound / Silent choice beside the part's controls, carried in the link, for when you'd rather play it yourself - Silent measured as zero guitar notes and the band's own level exactly.

summary: The suggested part sounded like a synthesizer, not the recorded guitar
detail: Reported 2026-09-11 ("It sounds like this is synth guitar. Can we use the samples?"). Measured rather than assumed: the part was on the recorded guitar all along - voiceUse showed every note from a sample - but a strum sent all six strings of the grip at one velocity, and the sum went into the limiter at 1.27 with 4.8 dB of reduction on every strum, which is the flattened, pumping sound of a limiter working, not a guitar. Single-note fill bars went in at about half that.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11. A strum's strings each play at vel x min(1, 1.45/sqrt(strings)), so six strings sum to about what two do (strumStringLevel in parts.js). After: 1.03 into the limiter, 3.6 dB reduction; a strum bar sits 1.4 dB over a fill bar rather than 2.8. The part's overall level is still partVolume's.

summary: The tab stopped following the bar being played, mid-progression, while the band played on
detail: Reported 2026-09-11 with a screenshot: playhead and lit name stuck on a C7 bar of a twelve-bar blues, everything else responsive, audio continuing. Cause: T59 stopped naming held bars, so the tab had fewer .tab-chord elements than bars, and followPart still indexed them by bar number - named[barIdx] - which named the wrong chord for a few bars and then read textContent of undefined at the first bar past the last name. The exception was thrown inside the animation-frame loop, before it re-armed itself, so the loop ended: the tab, the neck's following and the chart highlight all stood still from that bar while the scheduler, on its own timer, played on.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11. Every name in the tab carries data-bar, and showPartBar lights the nearest name at or before the bar being played. The follower is also wrapped in a try/catch that logs once, so nothing the part does can end the chart's loop again. Test: a progression with held bars (A A A D D E D A) walked bar by bar through showPartBar must light the arriving chord's name at every bar and reach the end; with the old lookup restored it reported wrong names at bars 1, 2 and 4 and a throw at bars 5-7.

summary: The green halo stays on every dot answered right in earlier questions
detail: Reported 2026-09-11 with a screenshot: five questions into a C major pentatonic drill, the dots answered in questions 1-4 all still wear their green ring, so the neck fills up with halos as the drill goes on. Cause, from the code: respond() adds marks.right (ear-right on a dot) and never takes it off - resetRound() clears the right/wrong classes from the .ear-answer buttons, which the point-at-it design no longer has, and not from the .note-hit dots; the wrong and close marks are timed off after 700ms, the right one is meant to stay until the next question and doesn't go then either. Fix: resetRound() should also clear ear-right (and ear-close/ear-wrong/ear-outside, in case a timer is outrun) from every .note-hit in the shape. A test can answer two questions in a row and count the dots still marked.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11. resetRound() clears ear-right/close/wrong/outside from every .note-hit as well as the buttons' marks. The pointing test now ticks to the next question after a right answer and counts marked dots; with the fix removed it reports '3 dot(s) still marked'.

summary: Changing how many bars a chord lasts in Set up left the tab as it was
detail: Reported 2026-09-11: 'when I edit the chords in the set up popup, the tab doesn't refresh until I click chart then go back to part'. Reproduced with the measures select: the chord and quality selects go through renderAll(), which rebuilds the part, but the bars-per-chord select only redrew the chart and reset the cursor.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11. The measures select rebuilds the part (its signature already counts the measures) and writes the share state. Test: a held progression, the first chord cut from three bars to one, and the tab's names must move with it; with the rebuild removed it reported the old 0:A 3:D 5:E 6:D 7:A.

summary: After Set on a typed progression, the chord count and the chord/bars dropdowns should show what was typed
detail: Reported 2026-09-11 with a screenshot of the Set up sheet after typing 'G G G G G G G G C C C C C C C C' and pressing Set: the note under the field reads '16 bars, 2 chords', the count reads 2 and the slots read G.I x 8 bars, C.IV x 8 bars. Two readings, to settle with Jeff: (a) the sheet did not update at the moment of pressing Set and only caught up later (the screenshot would then be after the catch-up) - applyTypedChords goes through loadProgression -> setSlotCount -> renderAll -> renderChordSlots, so look for a path where Set is pressed while the sheet is open and the slot rows are rebuilt from stale state, or where the count readout lags; (b) the expectation is one slot per typed bar - sixteen chords of one bar each - rather than the runs collapsed into two chords held for eight, which is what loadProgression does by design (README: 'E E E E A7 A7 E E Bm7 Bm7 is four chords held for four, two, two and two'). If (b), the collapse should go or become a choice, and MAX_CHORDS (the slot cap) needs to allow sixteen.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12 by construction: the chord table is gone; the chart's own bars are the editor, rendered from the progression after Set, so what you see is what is set.

summary: The part tab drew as black boxes with no strings after the genre examples were removed
detail: Reported 2026-09-11 from a phone on the live site: the tab under Part showed string letters, a chord name, and black rounded boxes where the fret numbers should be, no string lines. Cause: removing the genre examples (ddc082b) took their CSS block out of index.html, and the tablature rules (.tab-string, .tab-note, .tab-chord, .tab-playhead...) and the whole suggested-part block (.part-controls, .part-tab, .part-volume, .note-dot.sounding) sat in that block without a blank line between - the cut ran to the next blank line and took them too. Not caught because the suite checks structure and state, not computed styles, and the browser check after the commit looked at counts and console errors rather than at the tab.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-11 within the hour: the tablature and part rules restored under their own heading. Verified the computed stroke of .tab-string is the line colour again. Lesson recorded in the README's testing notes: a visual deletion gets a screenshot of what stayed, not only of what went.

summary: jazz Swing struck two chords at once on the last eighth before a change
detail: Found 2026-09-12 in the audio review: the resolved Swing pattern has a comp entry on slot 11 and compAnticipate, and scheduleSlot played both — the current chord and the next — together on every changing bar. Only that feel had both.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the push takes its slot, with the pattern's own length and weight when it has a strike there, in place of it. A test walks every resolved feel on a changing bar and fails if any slot strikes the comp twice.

summary: The count-in and the Simple click played the hi-hat at 1.0, five decibels over the band's loudest hat
detail: Found 2026-09-12: playHiHat with no velocity is 1.0; the band's accented hat is 0.55.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: CLICK = { downbeat: band HAT.accent, other: 0.4 } for both; a test holds them at or under the hat level with a downbeat accent.

summary: A hidden tab stuttered once a second
detail: Found 2026-09-12: background timers are clamped to a second and the queue held 0.4 s, so each slow tick found it empty and the progression slipped. Same in the parts and review players.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: audio.scheduleAhead(hidden) — 0.4 s visible (T36 kept), 1.25 s hidden — used by all three schedulers, each refilling at once on going hidden, before the first slow tick. A test pins the two values.

summary: The part ducked the band: one compressor for both buses
detail: Found 2026-09-12 in the audio review: the part bus and the band bus met at one compressor (-10 dB, 6:1, 120 ms release), so every part strum pulled the band down and let it back over 120 ms — pumping. Measured on two bars of Rock with a five-string strum every beat: the band lost 0.81 dB in the 150 ms after each strum, 2.07 dB at the peak.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: each bus holds its own peaks with a gentle compressor of its own, and the shared stage is a soft clipper (no makeup, no time constants); the buses trimmed by measurement to within a tenth of a decibel of where they sat. After: 0.05 dB after a strum, 1.12 dB at the peak. The old chain stays in the engine (dynamics: shared) as the reference the test measures against; the test caught the split undone.

summary: The parts' vibrato flag never reached the engine; bends never released; a palm mute was only a filter; a string could sound two notes
detail: Found 2026-09-12 in the audio review: `vib` was drawn in the tab and dropped by the player; a bend ramped up and stayed there whatever its length; mute was a 900 Hz lowpass with the same pick and the same ring; a re-struck string, a hammer-on's first note and a tremolo's last pick all rang under the note that followed; the slapback was a second pick with its own attack.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12 (sound phase 4): vibrato is an LFO on the playback rate (5.2-6 Hz, about a quarter of a semitone, arriving once the note has spoken); a bend held past 0.6 s comes back over its last quarter and `release` asks for it at any length (pitchPlan, pure); a palm mute is a lowpass sweeping 1600 to 700 Hz, a shade quieter, over in 0.18 s; one string sounds one note — the next note on it damps the one before in 12 ms (claim, keyed by the string, per graph); the slapback is a delay on the part bus (110 ms, darkened, one quieter repeat) that a pluck sends to. Measured offline: a muted pluck is over 100 dB down a quarter of a second on where an open one is 7 dB down; a note taken over leaves nothing of its ring; the repeat arrives 110 ms on, quieter. Tests caught each of four breaks.

summary: Every hat and snare hit was the same waveform; the rim and the ghost were quiet snares; no hat choke; no beater on the kick
detail: Found 2026-09-12 in the audio review: every noise voice read the same half-second buffer from its start, so every hat and every snare was the identical waveform (two hats measured sample for sample: no difference); a closed hat never stopped an open one; the kick was a sine with no beater; the rim and the ghost were the snare at a lower velocity; the ride was a hat with a 640 Hz square wave in it.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12 (sound phase 5): the noise buffer is two seconds and every voice starts somewhere else in it, its filter and its length a shade off, from a random stream of the kit's own (so the guitar renders the same with or without the band); a closed hat chokes an open one through the string registry (kit:hat, 30 ms; measured 30 dB of the ring gone); the kick has a beater (a few milliseconds of noise above 3 kHz); the rim is a knock and a ping with no body (2.7% of the snare's energy below 800 Hz); the ghost is the snare's stroke short and faint; the ride is five inharmonic partials over a bandpassed wash; band.js passes the kind. Tests caught each of five breaks.

summary: The room had no walls; the guitar comp sat 4.8 dB under the piano comp; the lone root was lifted by eye
detail: Found 2026-09-12 in the audio review: the reverb impulse was decaying noise from the first sample — no pre-delay, no early reflections, so the room had a size but no walls. Switching the comp voice from piano to guitar dropped the band by 4.8 dB (measured over a half-second strike on four chords) because the strum shares its level across its strings and the recordings fall away faster than the piano. The roots-only lift (1.9) was set by ear.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12 (sound phase 6): the impulse is silent for 10 ms, then five reflections between 12 and 41 ms each louder on one side, with the diffuse tail building from 28 ms over 40 ms; a test reads the buffer (silence, a reflection 7 dB over the tail, a monotonic decay, each wall on its side); the tail measured within 0.6 dB of where it was so the sends stay. GUITAR_COMP 1.7 puts the guitar comp within 0.3 dB of the piano comp; ROOT_ALONE 1.8 puts the lone root within 0.1 dB of the triad over four roots. Tests caught each of five breaks.

summary: A part note without its recording played the piano on the band bus
detail: Found 2026-09-12 in the audio review: playPluck fell back to playNote when a guitar sample was not loaded, which put the note on the band bus at the band's level as a piano, dropped the technique (mute, slide, bend, vibrato) and left the string registry out of it. Every part note on a file:// page, and the first notes on an http:// page before the bank is warm, played that way.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12 (sound phase 7): synthPluck — two sawtooths seven cents apart through a lowpass that closes as the note rings — is the fallback, on the bus asked for, under the same envelope, techniques and registry as the recording (playPluck treats the two voices alike: an output, pitch params, sources to start, a stopper for the registry); SYNTH_PLUCK_LEVEL 0.27 puts it within 0.1 dB of the recording over the first 0.3 s of an E3. The comp keeps its per-chord piano fallback (T43). Measured with the bank emptied for the call (_withoutGuitar): the note is on the part bus, nothing on the band bus, the mute is over, a bend of a tone raises the pitch, the next note takes the string over. Tests caught each of six breaks.

summary: The stroked icon buttons (the link, the loop, the chevrons) drew as solid blobs
detail: Found 2026-09-12: the icon-button rule set fill:currentColor on every SVG in a .ib, and a stylesheet fill beats the fill="none" the stroked icons carry as an attribute, so a chain of two open links, the loop arrows and the fold-away chevrons were painted solid — the copy-link button looked like a blob rather than a chain.

summary: A part written for one progression could not be shared or linked to
detail: Found 2026-09-12 building the Hendrix deep dive: a part with `needs` (the Hey Joe walk-up, written for the cycle of fourths and no other progression) opens only with its preset loaded, and the share link carried the chords but never the preset — so a link to the part, which is what the deep dive's "Drill it in Practice" is, opened on the excuse instead of the part, and Copy link lost the preset for every progression.

Held by "a part that needs its progression" in js/tests-practice.js: the part stays shut over a typed progression, the excuse names and loads the preset, the link carries it and brings it back; failed with the write removed and with the needs check removed.

summary: A power chord in a window too narrow for its 5th came out on skipped strings (x-7-x-7-x-7)
detail: Found 2026-09-12 on the Hendrix page ("Power chords with the open strings", E7♯9 in a window of frets 5–8): powerVoicing looked for the root, the 5th and the octave inside the position window only, and when the window held the root (E on the A string at the 7th) but not the two frets above it, it fell back to a three-string strum of whatever chord tones the window had — which landed on the A, G and high E strings, a shape no hand plays as a power chord.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: a power chord is one hand shape, so the shape is looked for with the root in the window and the 5th and octave allowed two frets past it, those notes marked reach; only a window with no root at all falls back. The engine test realises E in a 5–8 window and checks consecutive strings, root in the window and reach on the rest; it fails with the reach step removed (4:7 3:6 1:5 comes back).

summary: Vibrato was written onto open strings
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner in a tab on the Hendrix page: a lead line's vib flag was applied to whatever note the interval landed on, and when that was an open string the tab showed "~" over a 0 — a shake no fretting hand can give an open string (the sweep counted four parts doing it, the 5–6 boogie among them).
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the flag is dropped when the note is at fret 0 (the note plays plain); the reading test and the sweep both fail on vibrato at fret 0, and did with the guard removed.

summary: A strum the window cut into came out on skipped strings
detail: Found 2026-09-12 measuring the Hendrix page after B65: 76 of its 576 strums, and 3,872 of 170,919 over the library's parts in a spread of keys and windows, put a three-string strum on strings that were not neighbours — gripIn keeps only the grip's cells inside the position window, and a window that cuts into a grip (Bm's A-shape at the 2nd fret in a 0–3 window, the "high" three of a 7th grip) leaves cells on the A, G and high E strings, which a pick can't sweep as a chord; a colour tone on top (add) could land a string away from the grip the same way.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: a swept strum keeps to neighbouring strings — the grip is completed a fret or two past the window, those notes marked reach, before the window's own cells are settled for; a colour tone sits on the string beside the grip's top one or is left out; a shell (which mutes the string between) and a fingerpicked part (which plucks) are exempt. The engine test realises Bm in a 0–3 window and an E7 with a 9th on top; tools/sweep.js counts swept strums that skip a string (0 over 138,240 realisations but the sharp9 grip's fallback, fixed with it). The page's 576 strums: 0 skip.

summary: The thumb's bass note went to a treble string when the window had no root on the bass strings
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner on the Hendrix page (the Bold as Love changes, F♯m in a box of frets 5–8): thumbCell found no F♯ on the E, A or D strings inside the window and gave up, and the strum fallback took the first root the grip had — on the B string, the highest string of the chord — so the "bass note" of the thumb-over figure sat above the split chord.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the thumb reaches a fret or two past the window for a root on a bass string (the A-shape's root on the A string a fret above the box, marked reach), then takes the 5th or the lowest chord tone the bass strings hold, and the strum's own bass and fifth voicings look at the bass strings before any other. Held by the engine test (F♯m, window 5–8: a root on a bass string, reached); with the reach removed the note came back as the ♭3 on the low E and the test fails.

summary: A 7♯9 or 9th chord strummed whole lost its colour
detail: Found 2026-09-12 building the drills tab: a full strum of E7♯9 (or any 9th) went through the CAGED 7th grip, x-7-9-7-9-7, which has no ♯9 in it — the note the chord is named for — so a chord picked as 7♯9 on the jam tab's shape picker, or typed into a drill, sounded as a plain E7 unless a part asked for the sharp9 voicing by name.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: strumCells plays a whole strum of a major chord with a ♯9 or a 9th as the chord's own grip (sharp9Voicing: x-7-6-7-8-x, x-7-6-7-7-7, root on the A string) whenever that grip can be had at the position, with notes past the window marked reach; otherwise the CAGED grip as before. The drills test holds E7♯9 to x-7-6-7-8-x; the sweep is unchanged.

summary: A 12/8 part's changes opened in the drills on a sixteen grid
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner: "B7–E9: the I and the IV of the slow blues" opened in the drills with its strums on the wrong slots — the pattern a page sends (pt=) carried the strums' slots but not the grid they were written on, and the slow blues part is written on twelve slots to the bar; read as sixteenths, the 9th-chord figure fell apart.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: a pattern in a link carries its grid up front (12:…) and the drill realises, draws and plays on that grid — in 12/8 for the slow blues. Held by the drills test (a twelve-slot pattern decodes, encodes back and drills on a twelve grid).

summary: A grip handed to the neck whole was traced in the order its notes were played
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner in the drills: the shape line on the neck zigzagged across the grip, because a chord-change drill hands the neck the cells it struck in the order they were struck and the line was drawn in that order.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the neck traces every grip low string to high, whatever order the cells came in.

summary: A trill's repeats were drawn on the Hendrix and parts pages, the fret numbers on top of each other
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner: the 32nd notes of a trill had their fret numbers cut off. A trill is played as 32nds and meant to be written once (the first note marked trill, its repeats tabHide), but the example player's and the jam tab's note lists never passed trill or tabHide through to tab.js, so every repeat was drawn a quarter of a slot apart and the digits ran into one another.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the trill fields go through everywhere a tab is drawn, and a trill is written as one strike with "tr" and the fret it goes to (trillTo) over it, its repeats played but not drawn; the engine test holds the expansion to one written note carrying the upper fret.

summary: Staccato sixteenths were written as thirty-seconds
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner on the Hendrix page (the machine-gun lead): a note marked staccato is clipped to half a slot by the engine, and the tab's rhythm rule — a note that rings for no more than half its gap is written as its own value with the rest as a gap — read the half-slot as a thirty-second, so six repeated sixteenths came out triple-beamed.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the rule applies only to a note a whole slot or longer; anything clipped under a slot is written at the value its strikes are spaced at. Held by the rhythm test (four staccato sixteenths are one beat of beamed sixteenths).

summary: Play after a click into a stopped tab played nothing for a bar and then the wrong bar
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner: seeking into a stopped example on the Hendrix page and pressing Play gave silence. The player put the bar's start in the past by the slot seeked to, and its guard against a stalled clock — a bar whose moment has passed is stepped over — took that for a stall and skipped the bar, leaving the part-bar offset to land on the bar after.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the next-bar time is the moment the first slot played lands at, in the future, and a bar begun part-way counts its own start back from it; the same for a seek while playing.

summary: Notes went silent when a later strum or double stop on the same string had been queued first
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner on the Hendrix page (both notes of beat 2, bar 1 of the sliding-6ths card). The player queues a bar's single notes before its doubles and strums, so a double stop starting at slot 2 claimed its strings after a strum at slot 0 had; the string registry assumed claims came in time order and choked whatever it held at the newcomer's time — the later note, before it had begun.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: a claim is judged by when the notes sound, whichever was queued first — the earlier note gives way at the later note's start. Held by a sound test (a later note queued first is still heard).

summary: The neck drew a C7 voicing near the hand for the 7♯9 grip and named it the C shape
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner: on the 7♯9 cards the neck showed the C shape with its 7th (x-7-6-4-3-4) and a scatter of hollow chord tones while the tab played x-7-6-7-8-x. chordNeck took the nearest CAGED placement whatever the bar strummed.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: a bar whose strums are a grip no CAGED shape names (the 7♯9 and 9th grips, a power chord, a shell) is drawn as that grip and named as the tab names it; a CAGED bar is drawn in the shape its strums sit in before the shape nearest the window. Held by the example-player fingering test.

summary: One bar a row when a second nearly fitted
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner in the expanded view: the tab wrapped one bar a row beside the neck although a second bar would have fitted with the slots a little tighter, so a four-bar example took four rows.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: where only one bar fits at 24 px a slot and two would at 16 px or more, the slots squeeze so two share a row. Held by the two-bars-a-row test.

summary: The E-shape minor barre and power chords were fingered middle and ring
detail: Found 2026-09-12 while putting the finder's fingering model under the tab: F♯m at the 2nd fret came out 1-2-3-1-1-1 and a power chord 1-2-3, because fingers went on in plain order from the lowest fret; a hand holds those with the ring and the pinky, as in the major shape with the middle lifted.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: each finger is the one its fret says, one a fret from the index, or the next on when that one is taken, falling back to plain order only when that would run past the pinky. The finder's baseline for F♯m is updated to 1-3-4-1-1-1.

summary: "Open in jam" and "Open in drills" opened at the practice tempo, not the card's
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the owner: a card marked 66 BPM opened the jam at 46. The review's practice tempo (70% of the card's) had been put in the links as well as beside the tempo on the card, so the jam played slower than the card's own Play.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the links carry the card's own tempo; "start at N" stays on the card as the tempo to slow down to.

summary: The triads reading and the shell voicing left a bar empty where nothing fitted the window
detail: Found 2026-09-12 by the sweep (node tools/sweep.js) while checking the psychobilly work, and present on the committed code: 'Upbeat chops (the second guitar)' (Blues shuffle) in the triads reading, key D♭, window 0–3, left bar 4 (A♭m7) empty in every seed, because no close A♭ minor triad on G-B-e sits inside frets 0–3 (the nearest is 4-4-4) and the strum was dropped rather than reached for. The sweep's four-entry cap had hidden the same fault in the shell voicing: 'Minor comp' (Minor blues) in E♭ and A♭ at the nut and 'Four to the bar, 6ths and 9ths' (Western swing) in eight keys left their shell bars empty — 100 empty bars across the sweep in all — because shellVoicing returned nothing when the shell sat past the window, where powerVoicing already reached.
resolution: Fixed 2026-09-12: the triads reading asks again a fret, then two, wider and strums the nearest triad with the notes past the window marked as a reach; the shell voicing tries the same stretch moved a fret or two along (moved, not widened — a shell found across a wider stretch spanned six frets), marks the reach, and falls back to the low strings of the grip there is, as the power chord already did. The sweep now realises 161,280 parts with no empty bar. Held by the 'triads reading and the shell reach' test, sabotaged both ways.
